# How do a plant and an animal get food?

<!-- STEP id="animals-digest" -->
## Animals digest their food

An animal eats food from many sources: a rabbit eats grass, leaves and vegetables. Animals have tissues that help them **digest** this food, which means breaking it down into simple parts that the body can take in.

<!-- STEP id="plants-make-food" -->
## Plants make their food

A plant does not eat. Its green leaves have tissues that use the energy of sunlight to make food from water and carbon dioxide, and this is called **photosynthesis**. The roots take in the water and minerals from the soil.

<!-- STEP id="different-tissues" -->
## Different ways, different tissues

**So the answer to the food question is No: the rabbit needs tissues to digest food, and the tree needs tissues to make food by photosynthesis.**
